name: @kitr/tauri
description: @kitr/tauri: the desktop platform with a Tauri shell. Rust project in platforms/<name>/src-tauri, typed commands and events, storage drivers, installers.

kitr.name: tauri
kitr.title: Tauri
kitr.summary: Ship the same app to Windows, macOS and Linux as a small Tauri binary on the operating system's webview.

platform.label: Rust + webview
platform.tagline: Windows, macOS and Linux as a small Rust binary on the webview the operating system provides. Downloads measured in megabytes, not hundreds of them.

highlights.title: Small and light
highlights.text: No browser ships with the app, so installers are small and memory use is low. The webview differs between Windows, macOS and Linux, so test on each.

highlights.title: Typed Rust commands
highlights.text: `defineCommands()` types your Rust commands for the app, and `commandQuery` turns one into a cached query like any other.

highlights.title: Events both ways
highlights.text: `useTauriEvent()` listens to events Rust emits, and `emitTauri()` sends one back. Both do nothing in a plain browser, so the web build is unchanged.

highlights.title: Checked before you build
highlights.text: Builds need the Rust toolchain. `kitr doctor` checks for it, and the Rust project lives in `platforms/app/src-tauri` for you to edit.

run: the Tauri window over the Vite dev server
tauri build: a native bundle per OS
